memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So they took soot from a furnace and stood before Pharaoh. Moses tossed it into the air, and festering boils broke out on people and animals. The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils that were on them and on all the Egyptians." - Exodus 9:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The magicians appear one last time, and it is a pitiful picture. They cannot stand before Moses because they are covered in boils themselves.

Once they had competed. Then they admitted their limits. Now they cannot even remain in the room. The counterfeit has not merely failed — it has become a casualty.

That is the trajectory of every rival to God. It looks impressive at first. Then it reaches its limit. Eventually it is undone by the very thing it claimed to control.

And there is something worth noting about these men. They served a system that oppressed slaves and defied God, and they suffered along with it. Attaching ourselves to what stands against God never ends well, however respectable it looks at the time.

Paul writes that all rulers and authorities were disarmed and publicly exposed by Christ at the cross (Col 2:15). Every power that once seemed unanswerable has already been shown up.

Do not envy what opposes God. It is on borrowed time.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I quietly impressed by things or people that stand against God?
2. What have I trusted that has already shown its limits?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from admiring what cannot last. Anchor my confidence in Christ, who has already won. Amen.
